n: Given in April 1829 shortly after Oliver Cowdery, a schoolteacher, arrived in Harmony and began serving as Joseph’s scribe. The Lord opens by announcing the great work about to unfold.
God’s word is living and powerful, sharper than any sword, cutting to the deepest part of a person. Oliver is told to take it seriously.

f.w: quick and powerful, sharper than a two-edged sword

n: The harvest image again: the world is ready, and whoever wants to reap souls should work with all their might while there is time, laying up eternal salvation.

f.w: the field is white already to harvest

n: Anyone willing to work in the harvest is called of God.
Ask and receive; knock and it will be opened. The Lord repeats this promise often to early Church members.

f.w: if you will ask of me you shall receive

n: Since Oliver asked, the Lord tells him to keep the commandments and help establish Zion — a holy community of God’s people.

f.g: the work of building a righteous, unified people of God.

n: Seek wisdom instead of riches; then God’s mysteries will open to you, and you will be truly rich. Eternal life is the greatest wealth.

f.w: Seek not for riches but for wisdom

n: God will grant Oliver according to his desires. If he wishes, he can do much good in his generation.

f.w: even as you desire of me so it shall be unto you

n: Oliver’s message should center on repentance, and he should help bring forth God’s work.

f.w: Say nothing but repentance unto this generation

n: Oliver has a spiritual gift; he is reminded it is sacred and comes from God. D&C 8 later describes it as the gift of revelation and of working with the “rod.”
If Oliver inquires, he will learn great mysteries and can use his gift to bring many to the truth.
Oliver should share his gift only with those who share his faith, and must not treat sacred things lightly.

f.g: to treat carelessly or as unimportant.

n: If Oliver does good and endures faithfully, he will be saved — and salvation is the greatest of all God’s gifts.

f.w: there is no gift greater than the gift of salvation

n: The Lord commends Oliver for inquiring. Every time he asked, the Spirit instructed him — and that is how he came to be where he is.
Oliver had asked God and received enlightenment; the Lord now confirms that it came from the Spirit of truth.
Only God knows a person’s private thoughts and intentions — so this revelation’s knowledge of Oliver’s experience is itself a witness.

f.w: none else save God that knowest thy thoughts

n: The Lord witnesses to Oliver that the work he has been writing as scribe — the Book of Mormon translation — is true.
Oliver is to be diligent and stand loyally by Joseph through every hardship that comes for the sake of God’s word.
Oliver and Joseph should correct each other kindly when needed. The Lord also asks Oliver to be patient, serious, self-controlled, and full of faith, hope, and charity.

f.g: to warn or counsel gently but firmly.

n: Calling him by name, the Lord tells Oliver to treasure these words and promises to encircle him in the arms of his love.

f.w: encircle thee in the arms of my love

n: The speaker identifies himself: Jesus Christ, the Son of God, who came to his own people and was rejected, the light shining in darkness.

f.w: I am the same that came unto mine own, and mine own received me not

f.g: understands; can also mean overcomes or grasps.

n: If Oliver wants further witness, he should think back to the night he prayed in his heart about the truth of the work — something he had told no one.
God spoke peace to Oliver’s mind then. What greater witness could there be than one from God himself? Peace is a key way the Spirit testifies.

f.w: Did I not speak peace to your mind

n: Since the Lord has revealed things only Oliver knew, Oliver has received a true witness.

f.g: Oliver had told no one of that prayer, per Joseph Smith’s history.

n: The Lord offers Oliver the gift to translate as Joseph does, if he desires it. Oliver’s attempt is addressed in D&C 8 and 9.

f.w: a gift, if you desire of me, to translate

n: There are other records containing much of Christ’s gospel that have been held back because of human wickedness.

f.w: records which contain much of my gospel

n: If Oliver has righteous desires — to store up treasures in heaven — he may help bring hidden scripture to light.

f.w: lay up treasures for yourself in heaven

n: Joseph and Oliver are given the “keys” of this gift. Two or more witnesses establish truth, a biblical principle.

f.w: in the mouth of two or three witnesses shall every word be established

n: If people reject their message, Joseph and Oliver are still blessed; their enemies can do no more to them than was done to Christ.
Even if they are treated as Christ was, they will dwell with him in glory.
If people accept the message, they will be blessed, and Joseph and Oliver will rejoice in the fruit of their work.

f.w: joy in the fruit of your labors

n: Echoing his words in Matthew, Christ promises to be with those gathered in his name — and he is with Joseph and Oliver now.

f.w: where two or three are gathered together in my name

f.g: united in purpose; agreed about the same matter.

n: Don’t be afraid to do good. We reap what we sow, so sowing good brings good in return.

f.w: whatsoever ye sow, that shall ye also reap

n: “Fear not, little flock”: even if earth and hell unite against them, they cannot prevail if built on Christ’s rock.
Echoing his words to the woman in John 8, the Lord tells them he does not condemn them; they should sin no more and do their work seriously.

f.w: go your ways and sin no more

n: One of the best-loved verses in the D&C: turn to Christ in every thought; don’t doubt, don’t fear.

f.w: Look unto me in every thought

n: The risen Christ invites them to consider the wounds in his side, hands, and feet — the proof of his atoning sacrifice — and promises the kingdom to the faithful.

f.w: the prints of the nails in my hands and feet
